notes: Microsoft Support explains that RAM holds active apps and files for faster access; installed capacity and workload both affect the displayed percentage.
Microsoft startup-app guidance supports disabling a recognized optional startup app through Settings or Task Manager and restoring it when needed.

Microsoft's clean-boot procedure is an advanced isolation method, requires administrator access, can temporarily remove functionality, and warns against changing advanced boot options without guidance.
RAMMap is an official Sysinternals analysis tool that separates process, cache, kernel, driver, and physical allocation views; it is not presented as a one-click repair.
The current Windows release health and public Windows message center were opened before writing. No broad July 2026 advisory was found that makes all high memory usage a known Windows 11 defect.

The Windows 11 25H2 and 24H2 release-health pages listed a resolved July 2026 performance issue limited to some Dell devices with a specific Intel driver; the article explicitly prevents readers from generalizing that issue to unrelated PCs.
Microsoft's Memory Diagnostic guidance requires a restart and is relevant when memory symptoms accompany crashes, blue screens, or other hardware signs, not merely a high percentage.
The article blocks RAM cleaners, random driver updaters, unknown repair software, unverified community commands, and beginner use of Registry, BIOS, or command-line repair steps.
